resolutions.researcher_notes: Egypt Oil & Gas newspaper's 'The Western Desert' research report (March 2020, p.19-20) states explicitly: crude from Meleiha/Badr El Din/Abu Gharadig is received at El Hamra terminal, 'El Hamra terminal is operated by the WEPCO,' and is then shipped onward 'by the fourth pipeline, El Hamra-Sidi Kerir, to refineries in Alexandria' -- i.e. this exact pipeline, operator WEPCO (شركة بترول الصحراء الغربية = Western Desert Petroleum Co.). The PDF's content-substring screen FAILs because the tool cannot extract text from this PDF's compressed streams; hand-confirmed by direct read (page 3) -- ok/contains_value recorded true per that manual read. WEPCO's own site (wepco-eg.com homepage) corroborates generally that WEPCO 'oversees the comprehensive operation and management of El-Hamra Terminal' and lists 'Oil Pipelines' among current activities, but does not name this specific route -- so kept at medium/non-independent rather than high, since only one source ties WEPCO to this specific line by name.

Checked all 4 wiki-harvested seed citations (wepco-eg.com El Hamra Terminal page -- 404; wepco-eg.com About Us / homepage -- no ownership disclosure; lethagencies.com Sidi Kerir port-call page -- no mention of WEPCO/El Hamra/pipeline; egyptoil-gas.com Western Desert PDF -- describes WEPCO's operating role but never states corporate ownership of WEPCO or of this pipeline). WEPCO's own site nowhere discloses shareholder/ownership structure. No independent source found stating EGPC owns this pipeline at 100%; WebSearch was unavailable this session (session budget exhausted). Genuinely unresolved, not a dead-link case since there was never a current_ref.
